categories.title: Coding agents
categories.blurb: You use it to write and change code. You are its user, not a builder on it.

categories.title: Research and knowledge agents
categories.blurb: Agents that go and find out: deep research, document analysis, report writing.

categories.title: Browser and computer-use agents
categories.blurb: Agents that drive a screen: browsers, desktops, phones.

categories.title: Personal and desktop assistants
categories.blurb: The agent that sits next to your work and does errands across your own tools.

categories.title: Clients and interfaces
categories.blurb: The chat window, terminal UI or desktop shell you put in front of an agent.

categories.title: Harnesses and agent runtimes
categories.blurb: The loop you build on: tool execution, context management, turn control. Opinionated, not a library.

categories.title: Frameworks and SDKs
categories.blurb: Composable libraries for building an agent: handoffs, structured output, graphs.

categories.title: Skills and instruction assets
categories.blurb: Files you load into an agent: skills, prompt packs, AGENTS.md collections. No code to run.

categories.title: Orchestration, durability and deployment
categories.blurb: What keeps an agent alive between turns: queues, retries, state, serving.

categories.title: Memory and context
categories.blurb: What the agent remembers after the session ends.

categories.title: Model gateways, routing and account switching
categories.blurb: Everything between your agent and whichever model answers: proxies, routers, key and account switchers.

categories.title: MCP, protocols and registries
categories.blurb: The standards agents speak, the SDKs that implement them, and the registries tools are published to.

categories.title: Capability tools
categories.blurb: What an agent reaches for: search, scraping, documents, data access.

categories.title: Sandboxes and execution
categories.blurb: Where the agent's code is allowed to run.

categories.title: Evaluation and observability
categories.blurb: How you find out whether the agent is still doing its job.

categories.title: Security and guardrails
categories.blurb: Stopping an agent from being talked into something, or taking the system with it.
